nodes.name: Generative model and latent-variable data process
nodes.statement: Dataset $\bX = \{\bx^{(i)}\}_{i=1}^N$ of $N$ i.i.d. samples is generated by drawing $\bz^{(i)} \sim p_{\bT^*}(\bz)$ then $\bx^{(i)} \sim p_{\bT^*}(\bx|\bz)$, where prior and likelihood lie in differentiable parametric families $p_{\bT}(\bz), p_{\bT}(\bx|\bz)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Each datapoint is generated by sampling a continuous latent z from a parametric prior and then x from a parametric conditional likelihood; both densities are differentiable in the parameters and in z.

nodes.name: Recognition model (probabilistic encoder)
nodes.statement: Let $q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)$ be an approximation, parameterized by $\bphi$, to the intractable true posterior $p_{\bT}(\bz|\bx)$; we call $q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)$ the probabilistic encoder.
nodes.statement_clean: The recognition model q_phi(z|x) is a learnable approximation of the intractable posterior; it acts as a probabilistic encoder mapping x to a distribution over codes z.

nodes.name: Probabilistic decoder
nodes.statement: The conditional likelihood $p_{\bT}(\bx|\bz)$ is called the probabilistic decoder, since given a code $\bz$ it produces a distribution over the corresponding values of $\bx$.
nodes.statement_clean: p_theta(x|z) is the decoder: given a latent code z it returns a distribution over the data x.

nodes.name: Variational lower bound (ELBO)
nodes.statement: $\log p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)}) = D_{KL}(q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx^{(i)}) \| p_{\bT}(\bz|\bx^{(i)})) + \mathcal{L}(\bT,\bphi;\bx^{(i)})$ with $\mathcal{L}(\bT,\bphi;\bx^{(i)}) = \mathbb{E}_{q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)}[-\log q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx) + \log p_{\bT}(\bx,\bz)]$.
nodes.statement_clean: The marginal log-likelihood decomposes as a non-negative KL between the approximate and true posterior plus the variational lower bound L(theta,phi;x).

nodes.name: ELBO, KL+reconstruction form
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{L}(\bT,\bphi;\bx^{(i)}) = -D_{KL}(q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx^{(i)}) \| p_{\bT}(\bz)) + \mathbb{E}_{q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx^{(i)})}[\log p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)}|\bz)]$.

nodes.name: Naive score-function gradient estimator
nodes.statement: $\nabla_{\bphi}\mathbb{E}_{q_{\bphi}(\bz)}[f(\bz)] = \mathbb{E}_{q_{\bphi}(\bz)}[f(\bz)\nabla_{q_{\bphi}(\bz)}\log q_{\bphi}(\bz)]$, which exhibits very high variance.

nodes.name: Reparameterization of $q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)$
nodes.statement: Express $\widetilde{\bz} \sim q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)$ as $\widetilde{\bz} = g_{\bphi}(\beps,\bx)$ with auxiliary noise $\beps \sim p(\beps)$ independent of $\bphi$, where $g_{\bphi}$ is a differentiable transformation.
nodes.statement_clean: A sample from q_phi(z|x) is rewritten as a deterministic differentiable function of x, phi, and an auxiliary noise epsilon whose distribution does not depend on phi.

nodes.name: Reparameterized Monte Carlo expectation
nodes.statement: If $\widetilde{\bz} = g_{\bphi}(\beps,\bx)$ with $\beps \sim p(\beps)$ realizes $q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)$, then $\mathbb{E}_{q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx^{(i)})}[f(\bz)] = \mathbb{E}_{p(\beps)}[f(g_{\bphi}(\beps,\bx^{(i)}))] \simeq \frac{1}{L}\sum_{l=1}^L f(g_{\bphi}(\beps^{(l)},\bx^{(i)}))$.
assumptions: $\widetilde{\bz} \sim q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)$ admits the reparameterization $\widetilde{\bz} = g_{\bphi}(\beps,\bx)$ with $\beps \sim p(\beps)$
conclusions: The Monte Carlo estimate $\tfrac{1}{L}\sum_l f(g_{\bphi}(\beps^{(l)},\bx^{(i)}))$ is differentiable w.r.t. $\bphi$

nodes.name: Proof of reparameterized Monte Carlo expectation
nodes.statement: By change of variables: $q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)\,d\bz = p(\beps)\,d\beps$, so $\int q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx) f(\bz)\,d\bz = \int p(\beps) f(g_{\bphi}(\beps,\bx))\,d\beps$.

nodes.name: Apply infinitesimal change of variables
nodes.statement: From $\bz = g_{\bphi}(\beps,\bx)$ deduce $q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)\prod_i dz_i = p(\beps)\prod_i d\epsilon_i$, i.e. $q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)\,d\bz = p(\beps)\,d\beps$.

nodes.name: Substitute into expectation integral
nodes.statement: Therefore $\int q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx) f(\bz)\,d\bz = \int p(\beps) f(\bz)\,d\beps = \int p(\beps) f(g_{\bphi}(\beps,\bx))\,d\beps$.

nodes.name: Conclude differentiable Monte Carlo estimator
nodes.statement: Approximate by Monte Carlo: $\int q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx) f(\bz)\,d\bz \simeq \tfrac{1}{L}\sum_{l=1}^L f(g_{\bphi}(\bx,\beps^{(l)}))$, $\beps^{(l)}\sim p(\beps)$. Since $\beps$ does not depend on $\bphi$, the estimator is differentiable in $\bphi$.

nodes.name: Univariate Gaussian reparameterization $z = \mu + \sigma\epsilon$
nodes.statement: If $z\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)$, set $z = \mu+\sigma\epsilon$ with $\epsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1)$; then $\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{N}(z;\mu,\sigma^2)}[f(z)] = \mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{N}(\epsilon;0,1)}[f(\mu+\sigma\epsilon)]$.

nodes.name: Three families of reparameterizable distributions
nodes.statement: Choices of $g_{\bphi}$: (1) tractable inverse CDF (Exponential, Cauchy, Logistic, Rayleigh, Pareto, Weibull, Reciprocal, Gompertz, Gumbel, Erlang); (2) location-scale families (Laplace, Elliptical, Student-t, Logistic, Uniform, Triangular, Gaussian); (3) compositions (Log-Normal, Gamma, Dirichlet, Beta, Chi-Squared, F).

nodes.name: Generic SGVB estimator $\widetilde{\mathcal{L}}^A$
nodes.section: 2.3 The SGVB estimator and AEVB algorithm
nodes.statement: $\widetilde{\mathcal{L}}^{A}(\bT,\bphi;\bx^{(i)}) = \frac{1}{L}\sum_{l=1}^L \log p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)},\bz^{(i,l)}) - \log q_{\bphi}(\bz^{(i,l)}|\bx^{(i)})$ with $\bz^{(i,l)} = g_{\bphi}(\beps^{(i,l)},\bx^{(i)})$, $\beps^{(l)}\sim p(\beps)$.

nodes.name: KL+reconstruction SGVB estimator $\widetilde{\mathcal{L}}^B$
nodes.section: 2.3 The SGVB estimator and AEVB algorithm
nodes.statement: $\widetilde{\mathcal{L}}^{B}(\bT,\bphi;\bx^{(i)}) = -D_{KL}(q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx^{(i)}) \| p_{\bT}(\bz)) + \frac{1}{L}\sum_{l=1}^L \log p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)}|\bz^{(i,l)})$, typically lower variance than $\widetilde{\mathcal{L}}^A$.

nodes.name: Minibatch ELBO estimator
nodes.section: 2.3 The SGVB estimator and AEVB algorithm
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{L}(\bT,\bphi;\bX) \simeq \widetilde{\mathcal{L}}^M(\bT,\bphi;\bX^M) = \frac{N}{M}\sum_{i=1}^M \widetilde{\mathcal{L}}(\bT,\bphi;\bx^{(i)})$ with random minibatch $\bX^M$ of size $M$.

nodes.name: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes (AEVB), minibatch version
nodes.section: 2.3 The SGVB estimator and AEVB algorithm
nodes.statement: Stochastic-gradient algorithm that jointly learns generative parameters $\bT$ and recognition parameters $\bphi$ by ascending the SGVB minibatch estimator of the variational lower bound.
input: Recognition model $q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)$ with reparameterization $\bz = g_{\bphi}(\beps,\bx)$, $\beps \sim p(\beps)$

nodes.name: Initialize parameters
nodes.statement: $\bT, \bphi \gets$ Initialize parameters (e.g. random $\mathcal{N}(0,0.01)$).

nodes.name: Main optimization loop
nodes.statement: Repeat until convergence of $(\bT,\bphi)$: sample minibatch, compute gradient of $\widetilde{\mathcal{L}}^M$, update parameters.

nodes.name: Sample minibatch and noise
nodes.statement: $\bX^M \gets$ random minibatch of $M$ datapoints from $\bX$; $\beps \gets$ random samples from noise distribution $p(\beps)$.

nodes.name: Compute gradient of minibatch ELBO estimator
nodes.statement: $\bg \gets \nabla_{\bT,\bphi}\widetilde{\mathcal{L}}^M(\bT,\bphi;\bX^M,\beps)$ via backpropagation through the reparameterized SGVB objective.

nodes.name: Update parameters with stochastic optimizer
nodes.statement: $\bT, \bphi \gets$ update with gradients $\bg$, e.g. SGD or Adagrad~\cite{duchi2010adaptive}.

nodes.name: Return learned parameters
nodes.statement: Return $\bT, \bphi$ once $(\bT,\bphi)$ have converged.

nodes.name: Variational Auto-Encoder with Gaussian prior and diagonal-Gaussian encoder
nodes.statement: Set $p_{\bT}(\bz) = \mathcal{N}(\bz;\bzero,\bI)$, let $p_{\bT}(\bx|\bz)$ be a Bernoulli or Gaussian MLP, and let $q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx) = \mathcal{N}(\bz;\bmu^{(i)},\bsigma^{2(i)}\bI)$ with $(\bmu^{(i)},\bsigma^{(i)})$ output by an MLP. Reparameterize as $\bz^{(i,l)} = \bmu^{(i)} + \bsigma^{(i)}\odot\beps^{(l)}$.

nodes.name: Closed-form Gaussian VAE objective
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{L}(\bT,\bphi;\bx^{(i)}) \simeq \frac{1}{2}\sum_{j=1}^J(1+\log((\sigma_j^{(i)})^2) - (\mu_j^{(i)})^2 - (\sigma_j^{(i)})^2) + \frac{1}{L}\sum_{l=1}^L \log p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)}|\bz^{(i,l)})$ with $\bz^{(i,l)} = \bmu^{(i)}+\bsigma^{(i)}\odot\beps^{(l)}$, $\beps^{(l)}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\bI)$.

nodes.name: Closed-form KL between two Gaussians (prior $\mathcal{N}(0,I)$)
nodes.statement: If $q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx^{(i)}) = \mathcal{N}(\bz;\bmu,\bsigma^2\bI)$ and $p_{\bT}(\bz) = \mathcal{N}(\bz;\bzero,\bI)$, then $-D_{KL}(q_{\bphi}(\bz)\|p_{\bT}(\bz)) = \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{j=1}^J(1+\log(\sigma_j^2)-\mu_j^2-\sigma_j^2)$.

nodes.name: Derivation of closed-form Gaussian KL
nodes.statement: Compute the two cross-entropy integrals $\int \mathcal{N}(\bz;\bmu,\bsigma^2)\log\mathcal{N}(\bz;\bzero,\bI)\,d\bz$ and $\int \mathcal{N}(\bz;\bmu,\bsigma^2)\log\mathcal{N}(\bz;\bmu,\bsigma^2)\,d\bz$ analytically and subtract.

nodes.name: Compute cross-entropy of $q$ with prior
nodes.statement: $\int \mathcal{N}(\bz;\bmu,\bsigma^2)\log\mathcal{N}(\bz;\bzero,\bI)\,d\bz = -\tfrac{J}{2}\log(2\pi) - \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{j=1}^J(\mu_j^2+\sigma_j^2)$.

nodes.name: Compute negative entropy of $q$
nodes.statement: $\int \mathcal{N}(\bz;\bmu,\bsigma^2)\log\mathcal{N}(\bz;\bmu,\bsigma^2)\,d\bz = -\tfrac{J}{2}\log(2\pi) - \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{j=1}^J(1+\log\sigma_j^2)$.

nodes.name: Subtract to obtain $-D_{KL}$
nodes.statement: $-D_{KL}(q_{\bphi}(\bz)\|p_{\bT}(\bz)) = \int q(\bz)(\log p(\bz)-\log q(\bz))\,d\bz = \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{j=1}^J(1+\log(\sigma_j^2)-\mu_j^2-\sigma_j^2)$.

nodes.name: Bernoulli MLP decoder
nodes.statement: $\log p(\bx|\bz) = \sum_{i=1}^D x_i\log y_i + (1-x_i)\log(1-y_i)$ where $\by = f_\sigma(\bW_2\tanh(\bW_1\bz+\bbb_1)+\bbb_2)$ and $\bT=\{\bW_1,\bW_2,\bbb_1,\bbb_2\}$.

nodes.name: Gaussian MLP encoder/decoder
nodes.section: Appendix C.2 (Gaussian MLP as encoder or decoder)
nodes.statement: $\log p(\bx|\bz) = \log\mathcal{N}(\bx;\bmu,\bsigma^2\bI)$ with $\bh=\tanh(\bW_3\bz+\bbb_3)$, $\bmu=\bW_4\bh+\bbb_4$, $\log\bsigma^2=\bW_5\bh+\bbb_5$.

nodes.name: Marginal-likelihood importance estimator
nodes.statement: Three-stage harmonic-style estimator that approximates $p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)})$ by sampling latent codes via gradient-based MCMC, fitting a density $q(\bz)$, then resampling.

nodes.name: Sample posterior via gradient-based MCMC
nodes.statement:
Sample $L$ values $\{ z^{(l)}\}$ from the posterior using gradient-based MCMC (e.g. Hybrid Monte Carlo) with $
abla_{ z}\log p_{ T}( z| x) = 
abla_{ z}\log p_{ T}( z)+
abla_{ z}\log p_{ T}( x| z)$.

nodes.name: Fit density estimator $q(\bz)$
nodes.statement: Fit a density estimator $q(\bz)$ to the samples $\{\bz^{(l)}\}$ produced in step 1.

nodes.name: Estimate marginal likelihood
nodes.statement: Resample $L$ posterior samples and return $p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)}) \simeq \big(\frac{1}{L}\sum_{l=1}^L \frac{q(\bz^{(l)})}{p_{\bT}(\bz)p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)}|\bz^{(l)})}\big)^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Derivation of marginal-likelihood importance estimator
nodes.statement: Multiply $1/p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)})$ by $\int q(\bz)\,d\bz = 1$ and rearrange via Bayes' rule to obtain $1/p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)}) = \mathbb{E}_{p_{\bT}(\bz|\bx^{(i)})}[q(\bz)/p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)},\bz)]$.

nodes.name: Apply Bayes' rule $p_{\bT}(\bz|\bx^{(i)}) = p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)},\bz)/p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)})$
nodes.statement: Rewriting yields $\int p_{\bT}(\bz|\bx^{(i)}) \frac{q(\bz)}{p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)},\bz)}\,d\bz$.

nodes.name: Monte Carlo estimate over posterior samples
nodes.statement: Approximate by $\tfrac{1}{L}\sum_{l=1}^L \frac{q(\bz^{(l)})}{p_{\bT}(\bz)p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)}|\bz^{(l)})}$ with $\bz^{(l)} \sim p_{\bT}(\bz|\bx^{(i)})$, then invert.

nodes.name: Full Variational Bayes AEVB (latent variables and parameters)
nodes.statement: Stochastic-gradient algorithm extending AEVB to perform variational inference jointly over latent variables $\bz$ and parameters $\bT$ via reparameterizations $\widetilde{\bz} = g_{\bphi}(\beps,\bx)$ and $\widetilde{\bT} = h_{\bphi}(\bzeta)$.

nodes.name: Initialize stochastic gradient
nodes.statement: $\bg \gets 0$.

nodes.name: Loop over $L$ Monte Carlo samples
nodes.statement: For $l=1$ to $L$, draw $\bx$ from dataset, $\beps\sim p(\beps)$, $\bzeta\sim p(\bzeta)$, and accumulate $\bg \gets \bg + \tfrac{1}{L}\nabla_{\bphi}f_{\bphi}(\bx,g_{\bphi}(\beps,\bx),h_{\bphi}(\bzeta))$.

nodes.name: Return accumulated gradient
nodes.statement: Return $\bg$.

nodes.name: Full-VB shorthand $f_{\bphi}$
nodes.statement: $f_{\bphi}(\bx,\bz,\bT) = N\cdot(\log p_{\bT}(\bx|\bz)+\log p_{\bT}(\bz)-\log q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)) + \log p_{\balpha}(\bT)-\log q_{\bphi}(\bT)$.

nodes.name: MNIST and Frey Face VAE experiments
nodes.statement: Generative models trained on MNIST (500 hidden units; 100 hidden units, 3 latent dims for marginal-likelihood estimate) and Frey Face (200 hidden units, Gaussian decoder with sigmoidal mean) compared to wake-sleep~\cite{hinton1995wake} and Monte Carlo EM with HMC; AEVB converges faster and reaches a better solution.

nodes.name: Wake-sleep algorithm (cited baseline)
nodes.statement: On-line learning algorithm for continuous-latent-variable models that fits a recognition model and a generative model via two separate objectives that do not jointly bound the marginal likelihood.

nodes.name: Monte Carlo EM with Hybrid Monte Carlo (cited baseline)
nodes.statement: EM-style inference with HMC sampling (10 leapfrog steps, automatically tuned to 90% acceptance) followed by 5 weight updates per acquired sample; not on-line, so not applicable to full MNIST.

nodes.name: Adagrad stochastic optimizer (cited)
nodes.statement: Adaptive per-coordinate stochastic gradient method used to update $(\bT,\bphi)$ with chosen global stepsize from $\{0.01,0.02,0.1\}$.
